children: Federal prosecutors have charged two former staffers at Robinhood Markets with fraud, according to a complaint filed Tuesday in the Southern District of New York.
The complaint alleges that the two defendants were working as engineers at Robinhood when they used confidential company information to trade perpetual futures on the trading platform Hyperliquid.

The former employees, Hefu Chai and Huaisong Xiang, allegedly used information in emails and Slack channels to buy perpetual futures linked to crypto tokens, ahead of announcements that those tokens would be listed on the Robinhood Crypto platform. The claim alleges the defendants each profited more than $50,000 from the trades.
Perpetual futures are a type of derivatives contract that trades at all hours and allows investors to pile on leverage. Unlike traditional futures, they never expire.
The defendants' attorneys couldn't immediately be reached for comment.
In a statement, a Robinhood spokeswoman said the company has "zero tolerance" for insider trading.

"We have robust insider trading policies and procedures in place," the statement continued. "We immediately investigated and reported this matter to law enforcement and regulators, and will continue to cooperate with their investigations."
